newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IMPLATS SEES TALKS ON BAFOKENG DISPUTE.
newsitem.headline: IMPLATS SEES TALKS ON BAFOKENG DISPUTE.

text.p: Impala Platinum Ltd announced on Tuesday that its relationship with the Bafokeng tribe had been restored to the extent that talks to resolve a long standing dispute between the two would soon take place.

Implats said it acknowledged that the Bafokeng legitimately believed and adopted the attitude that agreements in 1990 between Implats and Lucas Mangope, former president of quasi-independent homeland Bophuthatswana, in his capacity as trustee of the tribe were invalid.
Under the agreement, which covers Implats mines on Bafokeng land, the tribe was entitled to 14.9 percent of Impala's taxable income from current lease royalties.
The deal also extended in perpetuity previous agreements concluded on behalf of the tribe dating back to 1977 and 1986 which would otherwise have had to be renegotiated in 1993.

Implats said on Monday that a settlement offer made by the Bafokeng in February 1996 constituted a genuine attempt to restore the relationship on terms which the Bafokeng believed were fair and reasonable.

"Subsequent to the offer being made, reports have been published by Impala Platinum and remarks attributed to Impala Platinum which have been a major factor in the deterioration of the relatioship between Impala Platinum on the one hand and Kgosi Lebone Molotlegi II, the members of the Supreme Council and other members of the Bafokeng Nation on the other hand."
Implats said it deeply regretted that the relationship had deteriorated as a result of those reports.
